description.short_caption: H&E stain of skin biopsy showing non-septate thickened branching hyphae.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained section of skin tissue at 400x magnification. Prominent findings include thick, non-septate, branching fungal hyphae (indicated by arrows) within the dermis. Surrounding the hyphae, there is an inflammatory infiltrate composed of neutrophils and other immune cells, consistent with an infectious process. The morphology of the hyphae suggests a fungal etiology, possibly a Mucorales species.
visible_findings: pink and purple staining typical of H&E
